entry.title: Top Taskbar Bleed 1.0.0
entry.content:
Top Taskbar Bleed

When a maximized window sits under a top-docked taskbar, the taskbar gets a full-width color panel behind its buttons that matches the window's top edge (optionally as a gradient, for Mica title bars), so the window's title bar appears to continue up into the bar.

Requires a taskbar docked at the top of the screen (via the taskbar position setting on builds that have it, or a mod such as Taskbar on top for Windows 11). On other dock positions this mod stays idle.

How it works:

  • A tracker thread watches window events and finds, per monitor, the foremost maximized window (the first maximized window in z-order on that monitor - not necessarily the foreground window, so a small dialog on top of a maximized app doesn't cancel the bleed).
  • The window's top edge row is captured from the screen and reduced to its dominant color (so a bit of text or an icon can't skew it); that color is the panel and decides the taskbar theme. Pixels covered by another window - a flyout, a thumbnail, a tooltip, a dialog near the top edge - are left out, so floating windows never tint the bleed. Hovering a taskbar thumbnail (Aero Peek) bleeds the peeked window if it is maximized on that monitor and hides the panel otherwise, since the desktop is what shows through.
  • Experimental Gradient bleed: instead of one color, the dominant colors of four windows at 20/40/60/80% of the width - away from the app icon on the left, the caption buttons on the right and a centered title - become a horizontal gradient, so a Mica or gradient title bar continues into the bar (a flat one stays flat). A point that doesn't fit the rest (a toolbar reaching that far, a hovered control) is bridged from its neighbors. Off by default: apps that put content along their very top edge can still show it.
  • One panel per taskbar is inserted into the taskbar's XAML tree, above the taskbar background and below the buttons. The panel mirrors the edge: window changes (switching, maximizing, minimizing) are picked up from window events and applied on the next composed frame, and the edge is re-sampled in between - every Poll interval (250 ms by default) while it is static, every 25 ms while it is changing - so a title bar that recolors in place (focus fade, tab switch, app theme change) is followed frame by frame. With Windows animations on, a window being zoomed into place isn't committed until its edge has actually landed, so the panel never flashes the background behind it; with animations off the first sample is applied as is.

Supports multiple monitors (each taskbar follows its own monitor).

Settings: Poll interval (how often a static edge is re-checked; window changes are event-driven regardless), Excluded programs (executables whose windows should never trigger the bleed) and the experimental Gradient bleed toggle described above.

The panel is a regular XAML Border named TaskbarBleedPanel, so its shape can be styled with Windows 11 Taskbar Styler like any other taskbar element. Target Border#TaskbarBleedPanel and set, for example, Margin=4,4,4,0 or CornerRadius=8,8,0,0 (the panel's bottom edge meets the window, so the rounded corners are normally the top ones). Leave Background and Opacity alone - the mod drives those (the background is a gradient brush).

Notes

  • The taskbar's XAML tree is reached through taskbar.dll and Taskbar.View.dll symbols (downloaded by Windhawk on first run), not through XAML diagnostics, so the mod coexists with Windows 11 Taskbar Styler and other XAML-diagnostics consumers. The bleed applies as soon as the mod is enabled.
  • Cost: with a maximized window present, each poll is one small screen readback (a 1px-high strip) plus a window enumeration; it doesn't register in Task Manager at either rate, and the fast rate only runs during a transition. With no maximized window the poll timer is off, and window events are only acted on when they come from a maximized window or the window being followed, so tooltips, thumbnails and overlays cost nothing.
  • Windows that exclude themselves from capture (protected media, some remote-desktop clients) return no usable pixels; the panel then keeps its last color.
  • The 1px taskbar border line (BackgroundStroke) breaks the illusion; it is hidden while a panel is showing and restored when the panel hides.
  • Readability: a light title bar bled into a dark-mode taskbar leaves white labels on a light panel (and vice versa). While a panel is showing, the mod switches that monitor's taskbar to the theme that matches the bled color (light panel -> light mode, dark panel -> dark mode) and restores the previous theme when the panel hides. This is done per taskbar through XAML's RequestedTheme, so only the affected monitor changes and the system theme itself is untouched.

Credits

The taskbar-thread helpers (RunFromWindowThread, FindCurrentProcessTaskbarWnd) and the taskbar.dll XAML-root lookup are ported from Taskbar multi-row by m417z, licensed under the GNU GPL v3.0. This mod is published under the same license.

entry.title: Drag to Scroll 1.0.0
entry.content:
Drag to Scroll

Hold Ctrl + Right-Click and drag your mouse to scroll smoothly and naturally across desktop applications, including web browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), text editors (VS Code, Notepad++), File Explorer, and legacy Win32 utilities.

Key Features

  • High-Resolution Micro-Scrolling: Injects fractional wheel increments for fluid, trackpad-like scrolling in modern desktop apps and web browsers.
  • Legacy Control Detection: Automatically detects classic Win32 controls (e.g., standard list views, tree views, edit boxes) and routes discrete WM_VSCROLL line steps to preserve native line-by-line movement.
  • Hands-Free Cruising: Release the Right Mouse Button while continuing to hold Ctrl to let the page cruise automatically based on cursor offset. Cruising disengages instantly on keypress, mouse click, or Ctrl release.
  • Zero Zoom Interference: Dynamically masks Ctrl state during scroll dispatch so applications never accidentally trigger browser zoom or editor scaling.
  • Accidental Click Protection: Tapping Ctrl + Right-Click in place without exceeding the deadzone transparently passes through as a regular right-click.

Compatibility & Limitations

  • Packaged & Modern UI Surfaces: Certain modern Windows interfaces (such as the Windows Start Menu or some packaged store apps) do not process standard Win32 mouse-drag messages through the message queue and are not supported.
  • CAD & 3D Software: If you use software (such as Blender, AutoCAD, or video games) that natively binds actions to Ctrl + Right-Click, you can exclude those executables under the mod's Advanced tab in Windhawk.

entry.title: Live Update for Windows 11 2.0.206
entry.content:
Live Update for Windows 11

A unified, single-slot "Live Activity" widget injected natively into the primary Windows 11 XAML taskbar. Instead of running multiple separate taskbar widgets or external desktop overlay windows, Live Update multiplexes contextual activities into one compact taskbar slot with a native XAML flyout popup.

Overview: Media

Overview: RAM Alert

Overview: Device Battery & Bluetooth Battery

Overview: Sensitive Permission

Overview: Wi-Fi Hotspot

How this mod differs from existing mods

  • Native single-slot multiplexer vs. external overlays: Unlike Dynamic Island for Windows (which runs as a separate overlay window at the top of the screen), this mod embeds directly inside the native Windows 11 taskbar layout (SystemTrayFrameGrid / RootGrid) and shares a single compact slot across all active providers.
  • Contextual activity switching vs. single-purpose widgets: Unlike standalone media mods (Taskbar Music Lounge, Taskbar Fluent Media Player, Island Media Controls) or calendar-only mods (Lunar & Holiday Calendar), this widget automatically switches to newly started activities (such as media playback, power connection, timer start, or microphone/camera access) while keeping a Vietnamese lunar calendar & almanac as the idle baseline.

Features

  • Media: Shows album artwork, track title, artist, interactive seek bar, and Fluent transport controls for players integrated with Windows Global System Media Transport Controls (GSMTC), with session switching for up to 16 active sessions.
  • Battery & Bluetooth: Displays charge percentage, charging/discharging state, estimated remaining/full time, connected Bluetooth device battery levels, and a shortcut to Windows Power & battery settings (ms-settings:powersleep).
  • Windows Clock (status reader): Displays active Stopwatch, Timer, and enabled Alarm entries observed from the Windows Clock app, continuing to advance locally from the last synced state when the app is minimized.
  • Lunar Calendar, Almanac & Vietnamese Culture Index: Computes UTC+7 Vietnamese lunar dates, Can Chi, Nạp Âm, auspicious hours (Giờ Hoàng Đạo), and 12 Trực using the Hồ Ngọc Đức algorithm. Includes a monthly calendar view, Vietnamese holiday list, and a built-in Vietnamese culture topic index that opens reference articles in your default browser.
  • Privacy Activity: Passively monitors active Microphone (Core Audio), Camera (Media Foundation sensor monitor), and Location usage and lists the reporting applications.
  • Task Progress: Passively observes taskbar progress (ITaskbarList3) for File Explorer, browsers, and archivers to display ongoing transfers in one place.
  • Displays & Wi-Fi Hotspot: Shows active external monitors/projection mode (QueryDisplayConfig) and Windows Mobile Hotspot status/connected client count (NetworkOperatorTetheringManager).
  • System Alerts (RAM & Storage on by default; Temperature optional, off by default):
  • RAM & Storage (enabled by default): Alerts when physical RAM crosses 80%/90%/95% or when any fixed drive has less than 10% free space (listing the low-space volumes).
  • CPU/GPU Temperature (optional, off by default): Alerts when CPU/GPU temperatures from a local LibreHardwareMonitor web server (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/data.json) cross 70/80/90 °C.
  • OBS Studio Recording (optional, off by default): Connects to local OBS WebSocket v5 (ws://127.0.0.1:<port>) when OBS is running to display recording elapsed time and Pause/Resume/Stop buttons.

Quick toggles, positioning & notes

  • Taskbar position (root_left on centered taskbar, automatic tray_left on left-aligned taskbar): By default (root_left), when the Windows 11 taskbar is centered, the widget sits on the left side of the taskbar right after the native Windows Widgets button (or at the left edge if Widgets is turned off in Windows Settings). You can optionally enable Hide Windows Widgets button in left corner (appearance.hideWidgetsButton, off by default) to collapse the native Widgets button while using root_left and restore its original state when disabled. Whenever the taskbar is left-aligned (TaskbarAl = 0), root_left automatically falls back to the system tray (tray_left) so the Start button and app icons are never covered.
  • Right-click quick toggles vs. Windhawk settings: Toggles in the widget's right-click context menu save quick runtime overrides (ui.*) that take precedence over the Windhawk settings tab. Saving settings in Windhawk (or choosing Reset to Windhawk settings in the context menu) clears all runtime overrides.
  • OBS WebSocket password: The obs.password field is stored as a standard Windhawk mod setting, so it is included in Windhawk settings exports.

Optional local integrations setup

  • OBS Studio: Enable Tools > WebSocket Server Settings > Enable WebSocket server in OBS Studio (v28+), then enable OBS recording in the mod settings and match the port (default 4455) and password.
  • LibreHardwareMonitor (Temperature): In LibreHardwareMonitor, enable Options > Remote Web Server > Run, then enable Temperature alerts in the mod settings and match the local port (default 8085).

Compatibility

  • Supported OS: Windows 11 (build 22000 or later) with the native primary XAML taskbar.
  • Windows 10 and third-party replacement taskbars are not supported.

Tiếng Việt

Live Update for Windows 11 tích hợp nhiều hoạt động trực tiếp (Live Activities) vào một vị trí duy nhất trên thanh taskbar gốc của Windows 11.

Điểm khác biệt so với các mod hiện có

  • Tích hợp trực tiếp vào taskbar thay vì cửa sổ nổi: Khác với Dynamic Island for Windows (tạo cửa sổ nổi riêng phía trên màn hình), mod này gắn trực tiếp vào cây giao diện XAML của taskbar Windows 11 và dùng chung một ô hiển thị duy nhất.
  • Tự động chuyển đổi theo ngữ cảnh: Khác với các mod chỉ hiển thị nhạc hoặc chỉ hiển thị âm lịch, Live Update tự động ưu tiên hoạt động mới phát sinh (như phát nhạc, cắm sạc, bật hẹn giờ, dùng micro/camera, quay OBS) và hiển thị Âm lịch & Tử vi khi ở trạng thái nghỉ.

Các hoạt động hỗ trợ

  • Phương tiện (Media): Ảnh bìa, tên bài hát, nghệ sĩ, thanh tua và nút điều khiển nhạc hỗ trợ nhiều phiên phát cùng lúc.
  • Pin & Thiết bị Bluetooth: Phần trăm pin, thời gian ước tính, mức pin thiết bị Bluetooth đang kết nối và nút mở nhanh cài đặt Nguồn & Pin của Windows.
  • Đồng hồ Windows: Đọc trạng thái Bấm giờ, Hẹn giờ và Báo thức từ ứng dụng Đồng hồ Windows; tiếp tục đếm từ mốc đồng bộ cuối khi thu nhỏ ứng dụng.
  • Âm lịch, Tử vi & Danh mục Văn hóa Việt: Tính ngày âm lịch, Can Chi, Nạp Âm, Giờ Hoàng Đạo, Trực, lịch tháng và danh sách ngày lễ Việt Nam. Mục Văn hóa cung cấp danh mục chủ đề văn hóa Việt Nam và mở bài viết tham khảo trong trình duyệt mặc định khi bấm vào.
  • Quyền riêng tư: Hiển thị ứng dụng đang sử dụng Micro, Camera hoặc Vị trí.
  • Tiến trình tác vụ: Theo dõi trạng thái tiến độ trên taskbar của File Explorer, trình duyệt và phần mềm giải nén.
  • Trình chiếu & Điểm phát sóng Wi-Fi: Hiển thị màn hình phụ đang kết nối và trạng thái Mobile Hotspot cùng danh sách thiết bị.
  • Cảnh báo hệ thống (RAM & Bộ nhớ bật mặc định; Nhiệt độ tùy chọn, tắt mặc định):
  • RAM & Ổ đĩa (bật mặc định): Cảnh báo khi RAM vượt 80%/90%/95% hoặc khi ổ đĩa cố định còn dưới 10% dung lượng trống (hiển thị rõ tên ổ đĩa bị đầy).
  • Nhiệt độ CPU/GPU (tùy chọn, tắt mặc định): Cảnh báo khi nhiệt độ CPU/GPU đọc từ LibreHardwareMonitor Remote Web Server (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/data.json) vượt 70/80/90 °C.
  • Quay màn hình OBS (tùy chọn, tắt mặc định): Kết nối cục bộ (127.0.0.1) với OBS WebSocket v5 khi bật trong cài đặt để hiển thị thời lượng quay và nút Tạm dừng/Tiếp tục/Dừng.

Lưu ý về vị trí, menu chuột phải & mật khẩu OBS

  • Vị trí mặc định (root_left khi taskbar căn giữa, tự động về tray_left khi taskbar căn trái): Mặc định khi thanh taskbar Windows 11 căn giữa, widget nằm ở góc trái (root_left) ngay sau nút Các tiện ích (Widgets) của Windows để không chồng lấp (hoặc sát mép trái nếu bạn đã tắt Widgets trong cài đặt Windows). Bạn có thể bật tùy chọn Ẩn nút Các tiện ích (Widgets) ở góc trái (appearance.hideWidgetsButton, tắt mặc định) nếu muốn ẩn nút Widgets gốc khi dùng root_left (tự khôi phục đúng trạng thái ban đầu khi tắt). Khi thanh taskbar được căn trái (TaskbarAl = 0), mod sẽ tự động chuyển vị trí về khay hệ thống (tray_left) để không bao giờ đè lên nút Start và các biểu tượng ứng dụng.
  • Menu chuột phải và cài đặt Windhawk: Các tùy chọn bật/tắt nhanh trong menu chuột phải lưu trạng thái ghi đè tạm thời (ui.*) và được ưu tiên hơn trang cài đặt Windhawk. Khi bạn bấm Lưu trong trang cài đặt Windhawk (hoặc chọn Khôi phục theo cài đặt Windhawk trong menu chuột phải), các ghi đè tạm thời này sẽ được xóa.
  • Mật khẩu OBS WebSocket: Trường obs.password là cài đặt thông thường của Windhawk nên sẽ được bao gồm khi xuất (export) cài đặt Windhawk.

entry.title: Windows Key to Search 1.0
entry.content:
Windows Key to Search

Tap either Windows key to open Search instead of Start. Search opens when the key is released. Windows-key combinations such as Win+E, Win+R, Win+Shift+S, and Win+S continue to work normally. The generated shortcut is held for 50 ms before release.

By default, the helper runs without requesting administrator privileges. On Windhawk 1.7.3, administrator windows keep their normal Windows-key behavior. On Windhawk 2.0 alpha 4 or later, the mod requests UIAccess, which also covers administrator windows when that host is available.

The optional Support administrator windows on Windhawk 1.7.3 setting launches an elevated helper. It is off by default. Enabling it can show a UAC prompt at every sign-in, and after enabling or updating the mod. The prompt runs on a background thread, and an already-running helper prevents another prompt. If elevation is cancelled, the helper runs normally instead. Disable and re-enable the mod after changing this setting. On Windhawk 2.0, leave this setting off and use its UIAccess host.

The helper uses Windhawk's tool-mod launcher, with an optional background elevation path on older Windhawk versions.

Windows-key mouse gestures used by tools such as AltDrag or AltSnap are not supported: the mod withholds the Windows key until another keyboard key is pressed. UAC's secure desktop is outside the scope of the mod.

entry.title: Minecraft launcher region detection spoof 0.1.0
entry.content:
Minecraft launcher region detection spoof

Presents Singapore region information to PCL CE and HMCL to bypass their mainland China restrictions on downloading, installing and repairing Minecraft. The purpose is to give users the same choice of launcher features across regions.

Region and time zone

  • PCL CE: user region SG, Windows device region GeoID 215, and Singapore Standard Time.
  • HMCL: Windows user GeoID 215, JVM country SG, and JVM time zone Asia/Singapore. Existing user.country and user.timezone JVM options are replaced, and legacy user.region options are removed.
  • The affected launcher's time zone is fixed to UTC+8, without daylight saving time. Local times shown by the launcher use UTC+8 even when Windows is set to another time zone.
  • Language settings are preserved. Locale-dependent formats can reflect the Singapore region. The overrides apply within the target processes.

Target processes

Supports 64-bit x64 and ARM64 processes with these executable names:

  • PCL2_CE*.exe for PCL CE.
  • HMCL*.exe for HMCL executables.
  • java.exe and javaw.exe when the command line launches HMCL*.jar, a JAR embedded in HMCL*.exe, or the main class org.jackhuang.hmcl.Main.

Usage

Enable the mod before starting HMCL so that its region options are set before JVM creation. Restart PCL CE after enabling the mod to refresh its cached region and local time zone. To restore the original region behavior, disable the mod and fully restart the affected launcher.

Upstream changes

  • PCL CE #3673 introduces mainland China restrictions for Minecraft and modpack downloads, installation and repair, using Windows region, locale, language and time zone signals.
  • PCL CE #3676 adds the Windows device region as an additional detection signal.
  • HMCL #7017 introduces mainland China restrictions for game downloads.

entry.title: Windows 8 Network Flyout Restorer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Windows 8 Network Flyout Restorer

This mod restores the Windows 8-style network panel from the taskbar network icon. The panel provides access to Wi-Fi networks, wired connections, VPN connections and Airplane mode, where supported by Windows and the installed hardware.

This modification has been tested on Windows 10 21H2, Windows 11 24H2 and Windows 11 25H2.

On builds that still contain the legacy network components, the mod uses them directly and downloads nothing; the result is usually closer to the original Windows 8 panel, since the system's own providers are used. On newer builds, the required Microsoft components are downloaded from Microsoft's Symbol Server and verified with SHA-256 before use.

Note: This is a best-effort modification. The Windows 8 network flyout and its dependencies had been removed in Windows 11 24H2+ and the restoration is done within modern Windows' limitations.

Requirements

  • 64-bit Windows 10 (build 17763 or later) or Windows 11.
  • Windhawk 1.4 or later.
  • An internet connection for the first download, if additional components are needed.
  • Native ARM64 Windows is not supported: fallback artifacts are AMD64-only and the native component route is unavailable on ARM64 builds.

How it works

Compatible Windows components already on the computer are used when available. Otherwise, the required Microsoft components are downloaded from Microsoft's Symbol Server and kept in Windhawk's private storage. System files are not replaced. Compatibility depends on the Windows build; the panel may not work on every system.

Downloaded files are checked with SHA-256 before use. Damaged cached downloads are replaced automatically when possible. If verification still fails, the downloaded panel remains inactive rather than loading an unverified file.

Options

The classic network icon is optional and disabled by default. If enabling it causes Explorer to restart, leave it disabled and use the alternative network icon. The settings control the classic network icon, the optional Win+Shift+N shortcut and the panel language. The downloaded panel supports English, Italian, Spanish, French and Brazilian Portuguese. When built-in Windows components are used, their original Windows language is retained. Restart Explorer after changing the panel language.

Privacy and system changes

The mod does not create or modify entries in the live HKCU/HKLM registry and does not create system-wide COM registrations. In fallback mode, registry access needed by the legacy components is redirected to a private application hive loaded with RegLoadAppKeyW from a unique file in this mod's Windhawk storage. Each explorer.exe instance gets its own hive file, so concurrent Explorer processes do not contend for one backing file. The hive is not mounted under HKCU/HKLM and is not visible to other processes. On normal unload the mod closes the hive and attempts to remove its file; a crash can leave an orphaned hive file in mod storage. Downloaded components are also kept in Windhawk storage to avoid downloading them at every start.

If you used an earlier release, its HKCU\Software\Windhawk\Mods\win8-network-flyout-restorer\VirtualRegistry subtree (or the older windows-8-network-flyout-restorer name) may still be present. This release does not delete old registry data automatically; after all older mod/Explorer instances have stopped, remove those legacy entries manually if you want to clean them up.

Troubleshooting

If a handled C++ error occurs, the mod stops accepting requests for that session and attempts to shut down its features. Restart Explorer before trying again. This does not protect Explorer from every possible error in legacy Windows components.

If the panel does not open, check the internet connection and Windhawk's mod log. An SHA-256 mismatch is not ignored. Disabling the mod and restarting Explorer restores the normal Windows behavior. If shutdown gets stuck, some resources may be kept until Explorer exits to avoid unloading code that is still running.

Credits

  • AdministratoX - Testing on Windows 11 25H2

entry.title: DeepSeek Balance in Taskbar 1.0.0
entry.content:
DeepSeek Balance in Taskbar

Shows the current DeepSeek API account balance right in the Windows taskbar clock:

0:17
22.10.2026 | ≈1 058 ₽

Works in explorer.exe on Windows 10 and Windows 11 with the stock taskbar. Networking uses the built-in WinHTTP stack and JSON/XML parsing is hand-written, so there are no external dependencies.

How it works

  • The mod hooks GetTimeFormatEx / GetDateFormatEx from kernelbase.dll — the functions the taskbar clock uses to format its text (Windows 10: ClockButton::UpdateTextStringsIfNecessary, Windows 11: ClockSystemTrayIconDataModel::RefreshIcon).
  • Formatting is only decorated while the clock is refreshing (a thread-local flag), so dates in other Explorer windows are left alone.
  • A background thread polls https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance through WinHTTP, parses the JSON and updates the clock suffix.
  • When a display currency is selected, the mod fetches the official Bank of Russia rates (https://www.cbr.ru/scripts/XML_daily.asp, windows-1251), caches them for six hours and converts the balance. With the default native mode no such request is made.

Settings

  • DeepSeek API key — sk-... key stored in Windhawk's mod settings on this PC. Leave it empty to use the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable.
  • Refresh interval — how often to poll the API, in minutes.
  • Clock line — append to the bottom (date) line or the top (time) line.
  • Display currency — native keeps the currency returned by the API; CNY, RUB and USD convert the balance with the official Bank of Russia rates.

Notes

  • Requires symbols (PDB) for explorer.exe / SystemTray.dll; Windhawk downloads them automatically on first start.
  • The old Windows 10 taskbar on Windows 11 (ExplorerPatcher) is not supported.
  • The API key is stored in plain text in the mod settings: Windhawk has no secret setting type. The key is only sent to api.deepseek.com and is never logged; no other endpoints are contacted except www.cbr.ru, and only when a display currency other than native is selected. In a regular (non-portable) Windhawk install the settings are machine-wide, so every Windows account on this PC shares the same key.
  • Do not enable this mod together with Taskbar Clock Customization: both hook the same formatting functions of the clock, and that mod replaces the line text, so only one of them can win. Pick one of the two.

entry.title: Taskbar Icon Animation 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Icon Animation

When the mouse hovers over a taskbar icon, an animation plays on a transparent overlay above the icon (the overlay does not block clicks).

Effects

  • Heartbeat: Grows and shrinks twice in a "lub-dub" rhythm, with a red/pink halo flashing behind it.
  • Flash: White glow plus a lens flare, double flash.
  • Ripple: 3 rings spreading out from around the icon.
  • Neon glow: A rainbow halo that changes color.
  • Sparkle: Glints appearing randomly around the icon.
  • Bounce: 3 damped bounces.
  • Wobble: A damped side-to-side wobble.
  • Spin: A full rotation while growing slightly, with a ring appearing around it.
  • Jelly: A jelly-like squash and stretch that gradually settles.
  • Flip: Flips around the horizontal axis like a coin.
  • Shake: A fast horizontal shake.
  • Confetti: A burst of colorful confetti.
  • Bubbles: Soap bubbles rising from below the icon.
  • Love: A heartbeat plus hearts floating upward.
  • Random / Cycle: A different effect on every hover.

Notes

  • Works on both the Windows 10 and Windows 11 taskbar (button positions are found with UI Automation).
  • The mod runs in its own dedicated process, not inside Explorer, so a problem in the mod cannot crash the shell.
  • Animations are not played over fullscreen apps.
  • The animation is played on the overlay using a screenshot of the icon, so if the icon is very dark or the same color as the background, its edges may look soft.
  • When "App buttons only" is enabled, Start, Search, tray icons, etc. are not animated.

Görev Çubuğu İkon Animasyonu

Fare görev çubuğundaki bir ikonun üzerine geldiğinde, ikonun üstünde (tıklamayı engellemeyen) şeffaf bir katman üzerinde animasyon oynatır.

Efektler

  • Kalp atışı: "lub-dub" şeklinde iki kez büyüyüp küçülür, arkasında kırmızı/pembe halo yanıp söner.
  • Flaş: Beyaz parlama + mercek yıldızı (lens flare), çift flaş.
  • Dalga: İkonun etrafından yayılan 3 halka.
  • Neon parıltı: Renk değiştiren gökkuşağı halo.
  • Yıldız parıltısı: İkonun etrafında rastgele beliren ışıltılar.
  • Zıplama: Sönümlenen 3 zıplama.
  • Sallanma: Sağa sola sönümlenen sallanma.
  • Dönüş: Tam tur dönerken hafifçe büyür, etrafında halka belirir.
  • Jöle: Sıkışıp gerilerek sönümlenen jöle gibi esneme.
  • Çevirme: Madeni para gibi yatay eksende çevrilir.
  • Titreme: Hızlı yatay titreme.
  • Konfeti: Renkli konfeti patlaması.
  • Baloncuklar: İkonun altından yükselen sabun köpüğü baloncukları.
  • Aşk: Kalp atışı ve yukarı süzülen kalpler.
  • Rastgele / Sırayla: Her hover'da farklı efekt.

Notlar

  • Windows 10 ve Windows 11 görev çubuğunda çalışır (UI Automation ile düğme konumu bulunur).
  • Mod, Explorer'ın içinde değil kendi ayrı sürecinde çalışır. Bu yüzden modda bir sorun olsa bile kabuk çökmez.
  • Tam ekran uygulamaların üstünde animasyon oynatılmaz.
  • Animasyon, ikonun ekran görüntüsü alınarak katmanda oynatılır; bu yüzden ikon çok koyu/arka planla aynı renkteyse kenarlar yumuşak görünebilir.
  • "Sadece uygulama düğmeleri" açıksa Başlat, Arama, tepsi ikonları vb. animasyon almaz.

entry.title: Explorer Column View 0.43
entry.content:
Explorer Column View

Bring Finder-style column browsing to Windows 11 File Explorer. Follow a folder path across resizable columns, revisit earlier selections, and inspect files beside your folders.

In action

Native Windows styling, with folder columns and the audio Inspector:

Columns also follow your existing Explorer styling. See the customized Explorer screenshot; its glass appearance comes from the user's other customization tools.

Browse with a clear trail

  • Select a folder to reveal its contents in the next column. Choose a different folder earlier in the trail to replace the columns that follow it.
  • Start with one column and add only the columns you use. Drag a thin divider to resize a column live; the layout scrolls horizontally as your path grows.
  • Press Right Arrow to enter the selected folder's column and Left Arrow to focus the previous column. Folder double-click and Enter extend the trail.
  • Each Explorer tab keeps its own folders, selections, column widths and Inspector.
  • On supported Shell versions, Open in new tab targets the owning Explorer window; ordinary folder opening continues along the column trail. Open in new window keeps its native behavior.
  • Browse Home and This PC, local and network folders, and archives exposed by your Windows Shell providers, including supported ZIP, RAR and 7z folders.

Look closer with the Inspector

Selecting a file opens its Inspector after the folder columns, filling the remaining space. Prefer a sidebar? Enable Use fixed-width Inspector to dock it on the right and show folder details too.

  • File information, icons and registered Open with applications.
  • Image previews and installed Windows preview handlers for supported documents.
  • Inline audio and video playback for supported formats and installed codecs.
  • Scrubbable audio waveforms, with duration, sample rate, bit depth and channel information when available.
  • Playback starts when you press Play and pauses when its tab is hidden.

Turn columns on or off

With Explorer focused, press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V (the default) to switch column browsing across open and new Explorer windows and tabs. Change Toggle shortcut in the mod settings, for example to Ctrl+Shift+C or F8. Use Ctrl, Alt, Shift and/or Win separated by +, followed by a letter, digit, F1–F24, or a named key: Space, Tab, Enter, Esc, Backspace, Delete, Insert, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Left, Right, Up, or Down. Other keyboard virtual-key codes can be written in hexadecimal, e.g. Ctrl+0xBA. Names are case-insensitive; leave the setting empty to disable the shortcut. Invalid shortcuts fall back to Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V and are logged.

The shortcut only runs in Explorer, not while typing in an address/search/rename field or using Right Alt (AltGr). Extra modifiers prevent a match. Choose a combination that does not conflict with another Explorer command: the configured shortcut takes precedence there, but cannot override Windows-reserved shortcuts. It remains available to other apps. Enable columns by default controls the initial mode. Use Explorer's main sidebar or address bar to change the first column's location. Click Save settings in Windhawk to apply configuration changes.

Compatibility and limitations

  • Designed for Windows 11. The mod hosts native Shell views and follows existing Explorer styling; it does not include a glass theme.
  • Windows 11 context menus are available on supported x64 builds in the 26100 and 26200 families. Other builds and architectures use classic menus. Use classic context menus forces that fallback inside the columns.
  • Use a column's context menu or keyboard shortcuts for file operations. The hidden native view's selection is cleared before columns cover it. The outer command bar's New and Paste still target the original tab folder; its status bar can reflect that folder rather than the focused column. Selecting or renaming a new item there temporarily reveals native Explorer. Deselect it to return to the existing column trail and Inspector.
  • Home contents depend on Windows' Shell provider. Unavailable recent entries cannot be previewed. Unsupported virtual roots return to the regular native view.
  • Previews depend on installed handlers/codecs. Some archive providers expose folders but no file streams. Encrypted archives and playback inside archives require an external application.
  • Some metadata and document-preview calls run on Explorer's UI thread. A slow handler or unavailable network file can pause the window. Installed media codecs run inside Explorer; Enable inline audio and video can be turned off for setups with incompatible codecs. Slow providers can delay unload.
  • Other mods that rearrange Explorer's file area may need compatibility testing.

Troubleshooting

Refresh views after navigation and resizing keeps additional redraw recovery enabled. If another styling mod causes excessive flashing, compare with it off.

entry.title: File Explorer Terminal Admin Aliases 1.0.4
entry.content:
🛠️ File Explorer Terminal Admin Aliases

Launch elevated (Administrator) command prompts, Windows Terminal, PowerShell, or custom shells directly from any Windows File Explorer address bar, opened to your active directory.

Just like typing cmd, wt, or powershell into File Explorer—but with administrator privileges and completely customizable aliases!

⚡ Features

  • Configurable Aliases: Choose any alias trigger you want (cmda, wta, psa, pwsha, basha, or your own custom commands).
  • Native & Silent Elevation: Intercepts shell execution directly inside File Explorer and launches with native runas elevation—no background PowerShell spawns, no .bat files, and zero flickering.
  • Zero PATH Pollution: Works without needing to edit your system/user Path environment variable.
  • Directory Preservation: Accurately preserves the active directory in elevated sessions, handling spaces, special characters, drive roots, and network UNC paths.
  • Virtual Folder Fallback: Automatically defaults to %USERPROFILE% when launched from virtual folders (e.g., "This PC", "Quick Access", or "Home").
  • Clean UAC Cancellation: If you cancel or dismiss the UAC prompt, the mod cleanly suppresses the annoying "Windows cannot find…" error dialog.
  • Inline Arguments Supported: Type extra arguments directly in the address bar (e.g. cmda dir or wta -p PowerShell).

⚙️ Configuration

Open the mod's Settings tab in Windhawk to:

  1. Customize aliases for Command Prompt, Windows Terminal, PowerShell 5.1, PowerShell 7+, and Git Bash.
  2. Toggle elevation (runas) on or off per shell.
  3. Configure custom aliases for any tool (e.g. code, wsl, nvim).
  4. Set an optional profile name for Windows Terminal.

entry.title: Taskbar Calendar Week Numbers 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Calendar Week Numbers

Adds a week number column to the calendar flyout that opens when you click the clock in the Windows 11 taskbar, like the week numbers in Outlook.

Settings

  • Week numbering: ISO 8601 (default; used in Germany and most of Europe) or the first-week-of-year rule from the Windows regional settings.
  • Column header: text above the column. Empty means automatic ("KW" for a German Windows display language, "Wk" otherwise). A single space hides it.
  • Week number color: the Windows accent color (default, the same color as today's date) or the normal text color.
  • Column width, font size and opacity of the week numbers.

Notes

  • Only the calendar flyout is changed. The mod writes nothing to disk and makes no network requests.
  • The calendar's day cells get slightly narrower to make room for the column.
  • The calendar flyout is hosted in ShellExperienceHost.exe. Tested on Windows 11 build 26220.

entry.title: DynamicDock 1.0
entry.content:
DynamicDock

Best for use with ultrawide monitors, but works on any monitor. Instead of the taskbar popping up in the middle of the screen, the taskbar appears or slides the icons to your mouse right where your mouse touches the screens edge.

This is still the real Windows taskbar, so everything works like normal: jump lists (right-click), hover thumbnails, badges, drag and drop, the tray and the clock.

Bottom taskbars (works with auto-hide or always visible)

  1. Choose how the taskbar shows:
    • Auto-hide: confirm or turn on Automatically hide the taskbar in Windows Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors > Select "Automatically hide the taskbar" from the menu.
    • Always visible: this mod also works with the default bottom taskbar that is always visible. Be sure to turn on Keep the bottom Windows default taskbar full width in the Bottom taskbar settings.
  2. Keep Taskbar alignment on Center.
  3. Move the mouse to the bottom edge of the screen anywhere: the bar opens under it or simply slides the icons to your mouse with the default taskbar.
  • Keep in mind that taskbars change widths based on the amount of icons in the bar. Some additional adjustments may be required as the total taskbar pixel count changes to maintain functionality and spacing as you desire.

Top taskbar

  1. In Windows Settings > Personalization > Taskbar > Taskbar behaviors, set Taskbar position to Top. This option only exists in recent Windows 11 builds (for example 26200.9711). If your build doesn't have it, use the Taskbar on top for Windows 11 mod to move the taskbar to the top.
  2. In DynamicDock's settings, open Top taskbar and turn on Taskbar on top of screen.
  3. Touch the top edge of the screen anywhere: the app icons slide under the mouse.
  • The taskbar itself stays full width across the top (Windows can't auto-hide it there), and the tray and clock stay at the right edge. Only the row of app icons moves, so nothing collapses or leaves empty space.
  • The center zone, limits, edge distance and smooth movement work the same. The icons never slide under the tray.
  • The Tray and clock and Rounded corners settings are for the compact bottom bar only and are ignored for the top taskbar option.

Full-width bottom taskbar

Prefer the taskbar to stay full width at the bottom too? Turn on Keep the bottom taskbar full width (in the Bottom taskbar section). The taskbar then works like the top one: it pops up full width with Widgets in the left corner and the tray and clock at the right edge, and only the app icons slide to the mouse.

Compatibility

  • Works with the default Windows 11 taskbar and with the Windows 11 Taskbar Styler mod (DynamicDock moves the bar; the styler keeps deciding how it looks).
  • Settings marked (default taskbar only) change the look of the plain Windows taskbar. When Taskbar Styler or a similar mod restyles the taskbar, those settings are skipped so they don't fight that mod's look.
  • Other taskbar mods (icon size, clock customization, auto-hide instant show, thumbnail reorder) can be used alongside it. Taskbar auto-hide instant show is recommended: it removes Windows' delay before the taskbar pops up.
  • Windows 11 only.

Troubleshooting (Try this if things are not working correctly)

  • The bar doesn't move, or the taskbar looks stuck in a moved position: turn DynamicDock off and on again in Windhawk. If that doesn't fix it, restart Explorer: open Task Manager, search for Windows Explorer, right-click Windows Explorer and choose Restart. This rebuilds the taskbar from scratch (it also closes open File Explorer windows). You may need to tap your windows key on the keyboard for the taskbar to reappear. Then return to windhawk and toggle your mods on/off as needed to function properly.
  • After installing or updating the mod, the first touch of the screen edge can take a moment while DynamicDock finds the taskbar.
  • To report a problem, turn on Debug logging on the mod's Advanced tab, reproduce it, and share the lines from the mod's log. You should see logs being created as you tap the screen edge in different places.

entry.title: Lock Screen Clock Styler 0.4.0
entry.content:
Lock Screen Clock Styler

Customize and enhance the Windows 11 lock screen clock with modern designs, frosted glass panels, dynamic date capsules, and clean layout controls.

Features:

  • Minimalist Sonoma (Clean Typography): Apple-inspired lock screen typography with date positioned above the time, slender display numerals, dual-layer atmospheric shadow, and bottom-left or center placement.
  • Modern Flip Clock: Split glass cards for hour and minute with an elegant horizontal flip seam.
  • Classic Flip Clock: Classic mechanical Solari-inspired flip clock with matte charcoal flap cards, aged ivory cream typography, mechanical split seam, and hinge axle clips.
  • Cyberpunk Sci-Fi HUD Terminal: Bespoke tactical Netrunner HUD terminal with dark obsidian glass chassis, tactical corner brackets in acid yellow and hot magenta, top telemetry diagnostic bar, electric cyan digits with rhythmic tactical pulse, and bottom telemetry date logger.
  • Retro Pixel / LED Dot Matrix Clock: Authentic dot matrix display inspired by classic digital boards with active and ambient inactive LED dots.
  • Minimalist Aura / Floating Clock: Frameless floating typography with ambient soft drop-shadow depth and an elegant frosted date pill.
  • Battery & Charging Capsule: Live battery percentage and power indicator (⚡ %85) for laptop users, automatically hidden on desktop PCs.
  • 12-Hour / 24-Hour Format: Switch between 24-hour time and 12-hour time with dedicated AM/PM indicators across themes.
  • Show Seconds Toggle: Optional live seconds display. Supported by every style except the two flip clocks.
  • Frosted Glass / Acrylic Styling: Translucent glass panels with subtle border highlights and rounded corners.
  • Dynamic Date Display: Elegant date and day capsule positioned beneath or above the clock, adapting to the user's system locale.
  • Hide Default Widgets: Clean up the lock screen by hiding MSN weather, sports, and news widgets.
  • Hide / Replace Default Clock: Seamlessly replace the stock Windows 11 clock with custom styles or adjust vertical offsets.
  • Extensive Customization: Card opacity, font size, vertical offsets, and alignments are fully customizable via settings.
  • No XAML Diagnostics: The mod walks the lock screen visual tree from its own UI thread instead of registering a XAML Diagnostics TAP. It can therefore run alongside other XAML-based Windhawk mods such as Windows 11 Start Menu Styler.

Screenshots:

entry.title: Enter to Rename in File Explorer 0.4.0
entry.content:
Enter to Rename in File Explorer

Use Enter to rename a selected file or folder in Windows File Explorer, like in macOS Finder. Press Enter again to confirm the new name. The standard F2 shortcut is unchanged.

Scope

  • Works only in File Explorer windows, not on the desktop or in file dialogs, and only when the keyboard focus appears to be inside Explorer's shell file list.
  • Does not intercept Enter while editing text, in the address/search controls, or with Ctrl, Alt, or Shift pressed.
  • This mod intentionally does not remap Ctrl+Enter to open a file.

Compatibility

Tested by the original user on Windows 11 for files, folders, rename confirmation, search, and multi-selection. Other Windows versions, Explorer extensions and alternative list controls have not yet been validated.

Notes

The mod intercepts Enter and synthesizes an F2 key press. The context check is based on Explorer window classes, which might differ across builds. If the mod causes unintended behavior, disable it in Windhawk.

entry.title: Refined Quick Settings and Sound 0.1.154
entry.content:
Refined Quick Settings and Sound

This "vanilla+" Windhawk mod reworks the Windows 11 "Quick Settings" and "Volume mixer" panels and makes them fit for daily use. It follows the Windows 11 design language, refining existing features and adding new ones: thin sliders, even row spacing at every display scale and a smooth frame transition to the Sound page.

Everything runs inside the shell's own panels (ShellHost): no extra windows, the system Acrylic, fonts, themes, lists, bindings and animations are kept, and customizations are restored when the mod is unloaded.

Features

Quick Settings

  • Brightness control for DDC/CI-compatible displays, with animated glyphs.
  • Press the brightness glyph to toggle night light on and off.
  • Open display settings directly from the glyph on the right side of the slider.

Sound

  • The "Sound output" page is now simply "Sound".
  • Change the output and input devices and the spatial sound provider from dropdown lists.
  • Below them, a reworked Volume mixer for the apps. It is collapsible and remembers its last state.
  • Mouse wheel on every slider; press an app's icon to mute and restore it, or its volume number to set it to 100.
  • Hide apps from the mixer by name (setting below).

Taskbar

  • Click the volume icon to open Sound directly.
  • The system's animated volume glyph and an Ethernet glyph for wired networks.

Compatibility

  • Windows 11 24H2 or later (Quick Settings hosted by ShellHost), x86-64 (ARM64 is untested). Development testing: build 26300, primarily at 125% scale.
  • Other Windows builds and display scales need validation. The mod depends on internal shell XAML elements and symbols which can change with Windows updates.
  • DDC/CI brightness requires a compatible monitor with DDC/CI enabled.
  • Added labels such as "Sound" and "Input device" are in English.
  • The first Sound opening in each ShellHost process starts with the mixer collapsed; subsequent openings remember its state.

Control Center discovery uses COM-interface symbol hooks in ControlCenter.dll and the public XAML visual tree; it does not open a XAML Diagnostics connection. Compatibility with other mods that edit the same controls still requires live testing. If the panel was already open when enabling the mod, close and reopen it; restart ShellHost if it is not picked up.

Notes

Disable other mods that change the Quick Settings, the Sound page or the taskbar volume icon before enabling this one. Errors are written to the Windhawk log.

Credits and license

GPL-3.0-only. The UI-thread dispatch technique follows m417z's Notification Center Styler (GPL-3.0). ControlCenter.dll discovery uses the COM produce-interface pattern documented by Per-monitor brightness. The hidden-applications parser is adapted from the local Sound Output Direct and Taller mod (GPL-3.0-only). The sliders-horizontal and ethernet-port icons are from Lucide (ISC); the license notice is included below in this source file.

entry.title: Mute Focused Window 1.0
entry.content:
Mute Focused Window

Press Ctrl+Alt+M to mute the app whose window has focus. Press it again to unmute it. Other apps keep playing.

This changes the same per-app mute as the Windows Volume Mixer, so the mixer shows the result and can undo it.

What gets muted

The mod mutes every audio session that belongs to the focused window's app, on every active output device. If some of those sessions are muted and others are not, the first press mutes them all.

Browsers and Electron apps such as Discord play sound from a helper process instead of the process that owns the window. The mod therefore includes the app's background child processes too. A child process with its own visible window is treated as a separate app and left alone. For example, a media player launched from a terminal keeps playing when you mute the terminal.

Hotkey

Change the hotkey in the mod's settings. Write any modifiers and exactly one key, joined by +, for example Ctrl+Alt+M, Win+Shift+F9 or Pause.

  • Modifiers: Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Win.
  • Keys: A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24, Space, Tab, Enter, Esc, Backspace, Insert, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Up, Down, Left, Right, Pause, ScrollLock, PrintScreen, Numpad0– Numpad9, VolumeMute, VolumeDown, VolumeUp, MediaPlayPause, MediaNext, MediaPrev, MediaStop.
  • Any other key: its virtual-key code in hexadecimal, such as 0x4D.

Windows gives a hotkey to only one program at a time, and other apps stop receiving that key combination. If the hotkey does nothing, another program may already own it. Turn on logging in the mod's Advanced tab to see why.

The default, Ctrl+Alt+M, also takes Word's Insert Comment shortcut. On keyboard layouts with an AltGr key, Windows treats AltGr as Ctrl+Alt, so AltGr+M (µ on German layouts) stops typing its character. Choose another hotkey if you need either.

Using the keyboard's Mute key

Most keyboards with a dedicated Mute key, and laptops with a mute function key, send VolumeMute.

  • Set the hotkey to VolumeMute to make the Mute key mute the focused app instead of everything. Also turn on Mute the system when there's no app to mute, so the key still mutes everything when you press it on the desktop, the taskbar, a File Explorer window or an app without audio.
  • Set the hotkey to Ctrl+VolumeMute to keep the Mute key as it is and use Ctrl+Mute for the focused app.

Keyboard software that reassigns the Mute key can stop it from sending VolumeMute.

Limitations

  • A browser is muted as a whole, not tab by tab. The Volume Mixer shows it the same way.
  • An app started from the focused app and hidden in the tray, with no visible window, counts as part of the focused app. For example, a music player started from a launcher and minimized to the tray is muted along with the launcher. Windows gives no reliable way to tell such an app from the hidden helper processes that browsers and Electron apps play their sound through.
  • Windows remembers an app's mute setting. An app you muted is still muted the next time it starts; press the hotkey or use the Volume Mixer to unmute it.
  • Pressing the hotkey on the desktop, the taskbar or a File Explorer window does nothing, unless Mute the system when there's no app to mute is on.
  • That system mute doesn't show Windows' volume indicator.

entry.title: Bulk Copy File and Folder Names 0.3.0
entry.content:
Bulk Copy File and Folder Names

Windows has Copy as path (Ctrl+Shift+C), but it gives you full paths in quotes, and often you only want the names. This mod copies the names of the files and folders you select in File Explorer as plain text, one per line. It works on one item or on many at once. A selection can mix files and folders.

Right-click menu

Right-click a file, a folder, or a selection of many files and folders in a File Explorer window. The classic menu gets two entries, Copy name and Copy name without extension. On Windows 11 they're in the menu you get from Show more options or Shift+right-click. The entries are on by default, and you can turn them off in the settings.

Copy name without extension keeps folder names whole, so sub.folder stays sub.folder, and a.tar.gz becomes a.tar. A name that starts with a dot, like .gitignore, stays whole.

Hotkeys

The hotkeys are off until you turn them on, so a fresh install takes no key away from File Explorer. To turn them on, open the mod's Settings tab in Windhawk, tick Hotkeys, and save. The defaults are Ctrl+Shift+Y for names with extensions and Ctrl+Shift+U for names without. You can change both keys there too.

A key is handled inside the File Explorer window that has the focus, so it never reaches other programs. It does nothing while you type in a rename box, the address bar or the search box, and it does nothing when no file or folder is selected. In both cases the key goes to File Explorer as usual.

If you pick a key that File Explorer already uses, like Ctrl+Shift+N for New folder, the mod wins while the hotkeys are on and something is selected.

Settings

  • Hotkeys: turn the two key combinations on. Off by default.
  • Modifiers and key for each copy action. Ctrl+Alt and Ctrl+Alt+Shift also match AltGr, so skip them if your keyboard layout types letters with AltGr.
  • Separator: a new line, a comma, or a space between names.
  • Quote names: put each name in double quotes.
  • Right-click menu: show the two menu entries. On by default.

Limits

  • The keys and menu entries don't work on the desktop or in file dialogs. Only File Explorer windows count.
  • The Windows 11 compact menu can't take new entries from a mod. Use Show more options.
  • The menu entries don't show on the column header menu, the menu you get from empty space in a folder, or the menu you get after a drag with the right mouse button.
  • Items that aren't files or folders, like drives in This PC, give their internal name.
  • If nothing is selected, nothing happens.

Tutorial

  1. Select the files and folders in a File Explorer window. A mix of both is fine.
  2. Hold Shift and right-click the selection. Pick Copy name or Copy name without extension.
  3. Paste. Copy name gives you every name with its extension, one per line.
  4. Copy name without extension drops the extension from files and keeps the full name of folders.
  5. If you'd rather use the keyboard, tick Hotkeys in the settings. Ctrl+Shift+Y then does what Copy name does, and Ctrl+Shift+U does what Copy name without extension does.

Gotchas

  • In step 2, the compact Windows 11 menu can't show the entries. Use Shift+right-click or Show more options.
  • In step 4, only the last extension goes, so archive.tar.gz becomes archive.tar.
  • In step 5, a key does nothing while you type in a rename box, the address bar or the search box, and nothing while no item is selected. File Explorer gets the key instead.

Credits

The way the hotkeys are caught, a hook on TranslateAcceleratorW that steps aside while a text box has the focus, follows the approach of the Explorer Custom Shortcuts mod.

entry.title: Fullscreen Start (Launchpad style) 1.0.0
entry.content:
Fullscreen Start (Launchpad style)

Replaces the Windows Start menu with a screen in the style of the macOS Launchpad: all installed apps in a grid, with search at the top and a blurred background.

Features

  • Fullscreen: takes the whole work area of the monitor where the mouse is, without covering the taskbar, other side bars or the Dock of the Standalone Dock (macOS-like) mod.
  • All apps: the same ones as the "All apps" list of Start (programs and Store apps), in alphabetical order, with icon and name.
  • Search: just type. The list is filtered instantly, ignoring case and accents; names that start with the text come first.
  • Adjustable blurred background: configurable strength, opacity and color.

How to open

Everything that would open the Windows Start menu opens this one instead:

  • the Windows key and Ctrl+Esc;
  • the Start button of the taskbar, or of the Dock of the Standalone Dock mod.

The mod hooks the function Explorer uses to show Start (XamlLauncher::ShowStartView in twinui.pcshell.dll), so the original Start doesn't open at all. Windhawk downloads the symbols of that file the first time the mod loads.

Keyboard and mouse

  • Type to search; Backspace deletes, Ctrl+Backspace deletes the last word, Ctrl+V pastes.
  • Arrows select an app, Enter opens the selected one (while searching, the first result is already selected).
  • Esc clears the search; with an empty search, it closes.
  • The mouse wheel or Page Up/Page Down scroll the list.
  • Clicking outside the icons or switching windows closes it.

Blur

  • Adjustable (default): the mod takes a screenshot the moment it opens and blurs it with the chosen strength. The background stays still while Start is open.
  • Acrylic and Windows blur: the effect is applied by DWM composition and follows what changes behind it. Windows doesn't allow changing the strength of that blur, so the strength setting doesn't apply to them.
  • No blur: only the color on top.

Changes to the settings apply the next time Start opens.

entry.title: Middle-click empty tab bar to open a new tab (Chrome/Edge/Brave) 1.0
entry.content:
Middle-click empty tab bar to open a new tab (Chrome/Edge/Brave)

Middle-click the empty area of the tab bar (between the "+" button and the minimize/maximize/close buttons) to open a new tab, just like clicking "+".

Currently supported browsers: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave. Other Chromium-based browsers may work too: add their executable in the mod's Advanced settings (custom process inclusion list).

The empty tab bar area is detected using the window's hit-testing: Chrome reports it as a caption (draggable) area, while tabs and buttons are reported as client area. By default, only caption areas that have a tab or a button between them and the side away from the window buttons are used, so the thin drag strip above the tabs and the area before the first tab are ignored. This also works with right-to-left UI languages, where the tab bar is mirrored.

Installed web apps (PWAs) are ignored, since they have a title bar instead of a tab bar.

The new tab is opened with the browser's "new" app command (the same command as Ctrl+T), so no keyboard input is simulated.

entry.title: Middle Click New Tab 1.0.0
entry.content:
The mod opens a new tab when you release the middle mouse button over the empty space of a tab strip.

Three apps are supported:

  • File Explorer: the new tab is opened by invoking the native AddButton (fallback: Ctrl+T).
  • Notepad: the new tab is opened by invoking the native AddButton (fallback: Ctrl+N).
  • Terminal: the new tab is opened by invoking the native AddButton (fallback: Ctrl+Shift+T). Note: This does not work if Terminal is running as administrator due to privilege isolation.

You can enable or disable each app individually in the mod's settings tab.

How it works:

  • The mod runs as a standalone Windhawk Tool, ensuring it executes in a single instance and doesn't inject multiple hooks into different Explorer processes.
  • A dedicated low-level mouse hook thread records middle-button press/release events. It never performs slow UI Automation work and never blocks global input.
  • If the press looks like it happened in a tab strip area, an isolated UI Automation worker thread verifies whether the point is on an actual tab, a button, or empty tab strip space.
  • If the mouse button is released before the check finishes, the mod temporarily holds the release event and re-sends it synthetically after the check. This avoids the race condition where the native app closes the tab before the mod can inspect it.
  • Middle clicking an actual tab or the add button is left untouched, so the native behaviors keep working perfectly.
